why_instrument_and_not_oracle: The developer's answer to section 9 of .agents/specs/ltx25-prompt-adherence.md, on that spec's own recommendation: the scorer never answers a question on its own. Every number it produces is consumed as a comparison against the #1864 render, which is the pinned ltx-2 oracle's output. Delete the reference and neither S1 nor S2 has a bound. So the ORACLE stays ltx-2, AGENTS.md's oracle table is unchanged, there is no .agents/oracles/ file for this checkpoint, and it is pinned by revision AND sha256 the way any other artefact this project loads is.
why_this_checkpoint: It is the checkpoint vLLM-Omni's own CLIPScorer defaults to (tests/e2e/accuracy/helpers.py:497 at a4ea67a21b20054dacc6e83952f9bd407e8ee4e7), and vLLM registers the family as a first-class runner (vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:251 at 5559679229, "CLIPModel": ("clip", "CLIPEmbeddingModel")). openai/clip-vit-base-patch32 is the recorded fallback with a stated reason: it is what vLLM's own tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_clip.py exercises. A swap between them changes every reading and must be recorded here.

weight_format_note: The only weight file at this revision is pytorch_model.bin. There is no safetensors sibling, so loading it unpickles. flax_model.msgpack exists and is not what transformers loads here.
context_note: MEASURED, not transcribed: config.json at this revision, sha256 eaf1c9089a8553c913d27ea66407f8bfc2be9989c80c9f331ddb3d63d4c5e8ad, 4104 bytes, has text_config.max_position_embeddings = 77 and vision_config.image_size = 224. About 75 positions are usable after the boundary tokens. A prompt that does not fit is REFUSED and never truncated: truncating produces a plausible number for a question nobody asked. The #1864 reference request is 13 words / 73 characters and fits. #1854's own motivating prompt, the 70-word golden retriever at scripts/ltx25-dit-attn-flash-pixel-ab.sh:697, does NOT: CLIP's own pre-tokenizer splits it into 81 chunks, and each chunk is at least one BPE token, so it is at least 83 positions with the boundary pair. That is a lower bound and needs no vocabulary file. So this instrument can answer the request the reference render was taken at, and cannot answer the one #1854 quotes. A 320x192 frame also reaches a 224x224 tower as a resized centre crop, so off-centre content is discarded.
gateable_note: MEASURED on 2026-08-31, not asserted. AGENTS.md's rule for an oracle applies to an instrument too: gateable only once it demonstrably builds and runs the model, and constructing a config proves nothing. What was run: the eight files below were fetched at the pinned revision and hashed, all eight digests verified, `transformers` loaded CLIPModel and CLIPProcessor from the local directory, and the scorer produced embeddings for the 25 frames of the committed #1864 reference render. S0 PASSED on that render -- the true prompt ranked first over the six committed decoys, per-frame 25 of 25 -- and the same scorer ranked the true prompt LAST on a pure-noise render, which is the instrument demonstrably able to say no. The end-to-end gate then FAILED that noise render on both adherence checks while C0 and both blockiness ratios passed it. The numbers are in .agents/specs/ltx25-prompt-adherence.md under `## Outcome`. This record does NOT carry the reference's per-frame distribution: S1's bound is recomputed from the reference on every run, and a copy of it here would be a transcription the gate could drift from.
download_authority_note: Given in session as "yes, download the checkpoint" and recorded in .agents/developer-preferences.md, in reply to a request that priced the artefact and named its three costs: 574.5 MiB across the eight files below, NO declared licence, and a pickle rather than safetensors. Fetched on 2026-08-31 at the pinned revision and hashed file by file; every measured size below equals the advertised one.
sizes_note: advertised_bytes and the revision are what the HuggingFace API returned to an unauthenticated request on 2026-08-31, and they agree with the reading .agents/specs/ltx25-prompt-adherence.md section 3 took on 2026-08-29. Every sha256 below is MEASURED on the downloaded file, and every file's measured size equals its advertised one. A digest that reads null would mean UNMEASURED, and the tool refuses the checkpoint while any is null rather than scoring with an unidentified file.
